$comment: Cold tier, and the widest blast radius in the whole configuration: an enabled server is a tool every agent that lists it can reach, and its catalogue travels with every request of that agent. Nothing is enabled by default. To enable one, move it from `disabled` into `servers` and fill in owner, trust, scope and version. harness doctor refuses an enabled server that is missing any of those, that carries a literal credential, or that still has a TODO in its command, args, owner or version.

cross-tk.$comment: The token-saving server the agents use where it returns less than a whole read: one symbol out of a large file, a workspace search, a summary. Its launch command is not known to the harness, so this entry is a template: fill in command, args and version from the Cross TK documentation your team uses before moving it into servers, and keep the name cross-tk, which is what the agent manifests (cross-tk/*) and the hooks match. The session start reports whether a server matching the name is declared here or in the user's profile; the crosstk-nudge hook reminds the agent once per large file that the server returns less; the crosstk-run hook routes tests, diffs and listings through the crosstk binary when it is on PATH. Nothing is mandatory and no tool name is written down.
cross-tk.command: TODO: the Cross TK launch command
cross-tk.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
cross-tk.trust: TODO: state what it reads and writes; a token-saving server usually reads the workspace and returns compact views of it
cross-tk.scope: workspace only, read paths only; anything that writes files or reaches the network needs its own line here
cross-tk.version: pin an exact version before enabling

github.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server

github.scope: use a fine-grained token limited to the repositories that need it, read-only unless a workflow genuinely writes
